title: Onboarding approval matrix, exception workflow, and license-compat scanning
creator: Aisha Choudhury
description:
Scope: Define an operational approval matrix and exception process that gates model onboarding based on automated license and provenance checks, restricted-weight detection, and safety heuristics; and ensure published performance profiles (latency/cost/quantization) are attached to each approved model version. This ticket drives the policy matrix, automation requirements for the license scanner, and the human escalation flow for exceptions.

Background: We currently ingest models and run a light license check, but there is no standardized matrix defining which licenses or encumbrances require manual review, nor a documented exception path. Customers have requested clarity on which models can be used in Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Security and Legal have requested a reproducible audit trail for approvals. We also need to make performance profiles a first-class artifact of onboarding so downstream routing and cost tooling can consume them.

Goals:
- Produce a clear approval matrix (auto-approve, auto-flag for review, block) based on license family, presence of restricted weights, and identified safety flags.
- Implement an exception workflow: who approves, expected SLAs for decisions, and record retention for audit.
- Expand the automated scanner to detect encumbered/restricted weights, license incompatibilities with usage tiers, and provenance gaps.
- Add model metadata schema changes to include pinned_versions, performance_profiles, license_summary, and provenance_url.
- Surface the license/exception state and performance profile in the Console and the public model catalog.

Out of scope: Full legal review of every license text (Legal will be consulted only for flagged exceptions), on-prem packaging delivery mechanics (handled by Private delivery).

Trade-offs considered:
- Conservative blocking policy reduces risk but increases manual review load and time-to-publish.
- Aggressive auto-approve improves throughput but risks compliance exposure. Proposed compromise: deterministic auto-approve for permissive licenses with clean provenance and no restricted weights; otherwise auto-flag and run the exception workflow.

Stakeholders: Product (Aisha), Legal (Marta Ruiz), Security (Devon Park), Infra/Serving (ENG-2123), Console UX (DES-219), Model Onboarding infra (ENG-2891).
acceptance_criteria: Approval matrix doc published in Confluence with categories: Auto-Approve, Manual Review, Blocked. Matrix includes license families, restricted-weights rules, and safety-score thresholds.
Automated license+provenance scanner runs on all new model uploads and writes a license_summary artifact to the model manifest (schema v2).
Scanner raises one of: PASS, FLAG, BLOCK and populates a human-readable rationale in the manifest.
Models that PASS are eligible for automatic publishing to the Hosted model catalog (subject to existing infra checks).
FLAGged models create a ticket in the Model Compliance queue with pre-filled context and a 3-business-day SLA for review; exception approvals must be recorded and linked to the model manifest.
BLOCKed models are prevented from public catalog publishing and placed into a quarantined state with remediation guidance.
Performance profile metadata (p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost-per-1k-tokens, quantization profile) is attached to the approved model version and surfaced in Console and docs.
Audit log for each decision (auto or manual) is retained for 3 years and exportable for legal/security audits.
API and Console display shows license_summary, restricted_weights flag, provenance_url, pinned_versions, and performance_profiles for every model version.

End-to-end smoke test: upload a model with MIT license and clear provenance -> automatic pass and published; upload a model with custom commercial license and closed weights -> flagged for manual review.
Security review completed and sign-off from Legal for the matrix and exceptions SOP.

risks: High manual review volume if many community models lack clear provenance or have ambiguous license text.
False negatives/positives from automated license parsing could allow disallowed weights into Hosted if not caught by other checks.
Performance profile collection may require additional infra work on benchmarking infra and allowed quantization runs which will extend timelines.
Customer confusion if models are auto-blocked without clear remediation guidance in Console.
